claims.statement: The Orc of Ebuda is a sea monster in Ludovico Ariosto's Orlando furioso; not a killer whale but a true monster, much like the one in the myth of Perseus and Andromeda.
claims.statement_id: Orca di Ebuda adalah monster laut dalam Orlando furioso karya Ludovico Ariosto; bukan paus orca, melainkan makhluk mengerikan yang sangat mirip monster dalam mitos Perseus dan Andromeda.
claims.quote: L'Orca di Ebuda è un mostro marino che appare nell'Orlando furioso di Ludovico Ariosto. Non si tratta di un esemplare di orca marina, ma di una vera e propria creatura mostruosa, molto simile a quella che appare nel mito concernente Perseo e Andromeda.

claims.statement: The Orc lives on the seabed by a rock of the isle of Ebuda (probably one of the Hebrides), whose piratical inhabitants feed it every young woman they capture.
claims.statement_id: Orca tinggal di dasar laut dekat sebuah karang di pulau Ebuda (mungkin salah satu Hebrides), yang penduduknya bajak laut dan mempersembahkan semua perempuan muda tawanan mereka sebagai makanannya.
claims.quote: l'Orca ha la sua dimora in fondo al mare, presso uno scoglio dell'isola di Ebuda (da identificare probabilmente con una delle Ebridi), i cui abitanti, dediti alla pirateria, offrono in pasto al mostro tutte le giovani donne da loro catturate.

claims.statement: These human sacrifices had gone on since ancient times at Proteus's command, after a king killed his own daughter, made pregnant by the sea god.
claims.statement_id: Pengorbanan manusia ini sudah berlangsung sejak dahulu atas perintah Proteus, setelah seorang raja membunuh putrinya sendiri yang dihamili dewa laut itu.
claims.quote: Il poeta inoltre precisa che tali sacrifici umani si protraevano da tempi antichissimi su imposizione di Proteo, a seguito dell'uccisione da parte di un re della sua stessa figlia, ingravidata dal dio marino.

claims.statement: Angelica, princess of Cathay, is saved by Ruggero, who rides the Hippogriff, stuns the Orc with his dazzling shield and breaks her chains.
claims.statement_id: Angelica, putri Cathay, diselamatkan Ruggero yang menunggang Hippogriff dan membuat Orca pusing dengan perisainya yang menyilaukan, lalu memutus rantai Angelica.
claims.quote: la principessa del Catai trova la salvezza grazie a Ruggero, che in groppa all'Ippogrifo stordisce l'Orca con il suo scudo abbagliante per poi rompere le catene che tenevano Angelica avvinta allo scoglio.

claims.statement: Orlando enters its mouth, wedges its jaws open with an anchor and kills the Orc with a sword stroke from inside.
claims.statement_id: Orlando masuk ke mulut monster itu, mengganjal rahangnya dengan jangkar, dan membunuhnya dengan tebasan pedang dari dalam.
claims.quote: dopo essere entrato nella sua bocca e averne bloccato le fauci con un'ancora,  il paladino riuscirà a uccidere l'Orca assestandole un colpo di spada dall'interno.

claims.statement: Its shape is more like a sea serpent than an orca, because Ariosto wrote that the Orc has no animal form except its head, and its skin is hard.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya lebih mirip ular laut daripada orca, karena menurut Ariosto Orca tidak berbentuk hewan kecuali kepalanya, dan kulitnya keras.
claims.quote: Forma bestiae potius similis formae serpentis marini quam formae orcinae est quia, ut ipse Ariostus scripsit, "Orca formam animalem, praeter caput, non habet" atque quia cutis monstri marini dura est.

claims.statement: Ruggero's fight with the Orc also appears in Gabriello Chiabrera's tragedy Angelica in Ebuda and inspired painters such as Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres.
claims.statement_id: Pertarungan Ruggero dengan Orca juga muncul dalam tragedi Angelica in Ebuda karya Gabriello Chiabrera dan mengilhami pelukis seperti Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres.
claims.quote: Il combattimento di Ruggero con l'Orca è presente anche nella tragedia Angelica in Ebuda del poeta barocco Gabriello Chiabrera e inoltre ha ispirato diversi pittori come Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres

claims.statement: Petermännchen ("Little Peterman") is a small, good-natured household spirit said to live in Schwerin Palace in Schwerin, Mecklenburg, Germany.
claims.statement_id: Petermännchen ("Peterman kecil") adalah roh rumah kecil yang baik hati yang konon tinggal di Istana Schwerin, Mecklenburg, Jerman.
claims.quote: Petermännchen (English: "Little Peterman"; German: [ˈpeːtɐˌmɛnçən]) is a small good-natured household spirit who is said to live in the Schwerin Palace in Schwerin, Mecklenburg, Germany.

claims.statement: The tiny spirit, perhaps only a few feet tall, is often described carrying many keys and roaming the vaults and tunnels under the castle, unlocking doors as he goes.
claims.statement_id: Roh mungil ini, mungkin hanya setinggi beberapa kaki, sering digambarkan membawa banyak kunci dan berkeliaran di ruang bawah tanah dan terowongan istana sambil membuka pintu-pintu.
claims.quote: The diminutive spirit, maybe only a few feet tall, is often described as carrying many keys, roaming through the vaults and tunnels underneath the castle, unlocking doors as he goes.

claims.statement: He is also the keeper and watchman of the castle, rewarding the honest and good while punishing or driving away thieves and intruders.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga penjaga istana yang memberi hadiah kepada orang jujur dan baik, sebaliknya menghukum atau mengusir pencuri dan penyusup.
claims.quote: He is also said to be the keeper and watchman of the castle, rewarding those who are honest and good. Conversely the spirit will punish or drive away thieves and intruders.

claims.statement: Petermännchen is also said to have woken soldiers who fell asleep on night watch to save them from punishment.
claims.statement_id: Petermännchen konon membangunkan prajurit yang tertidur saat jaga malam agar mereka tidak dihukum.
claims.quote: Petermännchen is also said to have woken soldiers who fell asleep on their night-watch in order to save them from being punished.

claims.statement: Legend says that when Christianity reached Schwerin, a pagan god worshipped where the castle now stands fled, leaving his spirit servants; all of them eventually left except Petermännchen, who would not abandon his post.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, saat agama Kristen tiba di Schwerin, dewa pagan yang dipuja di lokasi istana melarikan diri dan meninggalkan para roh pelayannya; semuanya akhirnya pergi kecuali Petermännchen yang tak mau meninggalkan posnya.
claims.quote: Legend further has it that when Christianity first came to the Schwerin area, a pagan god, who was worshiped at the site of the present Schwerin castle, fled leaving his servants, the spirits. Eventually these spirits also departed, except for one: Petermännchen, who would not leave his post.

claims.statement: Petermännchen is said to have tormented Wallenstein, granted the Duchy of Mecklenburg by Emperor Ferdinand II in 1628, so badly on his first night at Schwerin Palace that the general left the next morning utterly sleepless.
claims.statement_id: Petermännchen konon begitu mengganggu Wallenstein, yang dianugerahi Kadipaten Mecklenburg oleh Kaisar Ferdinand II pada 1628, pada malam pertamanya di Istana Schwerin sehingga sang jenderal pergi esok paginya dalam keadaan tak tidur.
claims.quote: Das Petermännchen soll unter anderem Wallenstein, den Kaiser Ferdinand II. während des Dreißigjährigen Krieges 1628 mit dem Herzogtum Mecklenburg belehnte, während seiner ersten Nacht im Schloss Schwerin so arg gepiesackt haben, dass der große General am nächsten Morgen vollkommen übernächtigt wieder abreiste

claims.statement: Richard Wossidlo interpreted some legends as making Petermännchen the god Radegast turned into a kobold, left behind to guard the sacred treasure of the Obotrites.
claims.statement_id: Richard Wossidlo menafsirkan beberapa legenda bahwa Petermännchen adalah dewa Radegast yang berubah menjadi kobold dan tinggal untuk menjaga harta suci bangsa Obotrit.
claims.quote: Richard Wossidlo deutete einige Petermännchen-Sagen so, dass das Petermännchen der in einen Kobold verwandelte Gott Radegast ist, zurückgeblieben, um den heiligen Schatz der Obotriten und die Angehörigen des Volkes zu schützen.

claims.statement: A statue of Petermännchen made by Heinrich Petters around 1856 stands on the castle's courtyard façade.
claims.statement_id: Patung Petermännchen karya Heinrich Petters dari sekitar 1856 terpasang di fasad halaman istana.
claims.quote: Eine von Heinrich Petters um 1856 geschaffene Petermännchen-Statue befindet sich in der Hoffassade des Schlosses.

claims.statement: The Piztia ('beast' in Basque), called La Pistia in Spanish, is a legendary wild beast that roams the woods around Domaikia in Zuia (Álava).
claims.statement_id: Piztia ("binatang buas" dalam bahasa Basque), dalam bahasa Spanyol La Pistia, adalah binatang liar legendaris yang berkeliaran di hutan sekitar Domaikia, Zuia (Álava).
claims.quote: La Piztia ('bèstia, fera, feristela' en basc), anomenada en castellà La Pistia, és una bèstia salvatge llegendària que vaga pels boscos dels voltants de Domaikia, a Zuia (Àlaba).

claims.statement: It is said to live in a cave on the Iruratxi crag of Mount Carrascal and to make children and livestock vanish; harmless by day, by night it devours everything it finds.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon tinggal di gua di tebing Iruratxi, gunung Carrascal, dan membuat anak-anak serta ternak menghilang; siang hari ia tidak berbahaya, tetapi malam hari melahap apa pun yang ditemuinya.
claims.quote: Es diu que viu en una cova a la penya Iruratxi, al mont Carrascal, i que fa desaparèixer nens i bestiar. No és perillosa de dia, però de nit es diu que devora tot el que troba.

claims.statement: Some speculate a real wild animal, such as a bear, gave rise to the legend, or that it is a local variant of the Tartalo or Anxo myth.
claims.statement_id: Ada dugaan legenda ini berasal dari hewan liar nyata, misalnya beruang, atau bahwa ia versi lokal mitos Tartalo atau Anxo.
claims.quote: S'ha especulat que podria tractar-se d'un animal salvatge real (un ós, per exemple) que hauria donat lloc a la llegenda, però també que podria ser una variant local del mite del Tartalo o Anxo.

claims.statement: In the 18th century, when Domaikia's turn came to lead the Mass at the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Oro, its prayers centred on ending the Pistia nightmare, and the surviving "Song of the Pistia" dates from that occasion.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-18, ketika tiba giliran Domaikia memimpin misa di Suaka Bunda Maria dari Oro, doa mereka berpusat pada permohonan agar teror Pistia berakhir, dan dari peristiwa itulah lahir "Lagu Pistia" yang masih ada sampai sekarang.
claims.quote: Quan li va tocar a Domaikia, les seves rogatives a la Mare de Déu es van centrar a demanar la fi del malson de la Pistia. És d'aquella ocasió que data el «Cant de la Pistia» que ha arribat als nostres dies.

claims.statement: The song opens by begging the Virgin of Oro to deliver them from the Pistia of Carrascal.
claims.statement_id: Lagu itu dibuka dengan permohonan kepada Perawan dari Oro agar melindungi mereka dari Pistia di Carrascal.
claims.quote: Soberana Virgen de Oro, líbranos de todo mal, te lo pedimos a coro, de la Pistia del Carrascal

claims.statement: Plafalgàs or Plafalgars, also called Pare Falgars, is a giant of Catalan mythology famed for his kindness, courage and prodigious strength, which he puts at his neighbours' service.
claims.statement_id: Plafalgàs atau Plafalgars, disebut juga Pare Falgars, adalah raksasa mitologi Katalan yang terkenal karena kebaikan, keberanian, dan kekuatan luar biasanya yang ia pakai untuk menolong tetangganya.
claims.quote: Plafalgàs o Plafalgars, també dit Pare Falgars, és un gegant de la mitologia catalana famós per la seva bonhomia, la seva valentia i la seva força prodigiosa, que posa al servei dels seus veïns.

claims.statement: The most widespread version places him in Vallfogona de Ripollès, as the tenant of the farmhouse of the same name near the hermitage of Santa Magdalena de Cambrils.
claims.statement_id: Versi paling umum menempatkannya di Vallfogona de Ripollès, sebagai penggarap rumah pertanian bernama sama dekat pertapaan Santa Magdalena de Cambrils.
claims.quote: La versió més estesa de la llegenda el situa a Vallfogona de Ripollès. Plafalgàs era el masover del mas del mateix nom, avui ja enderrocat, prop de l'ermita de Santa Magdalena de Cambrils.

claims.statement: The rector of Sant Julià gave him the task of carrying the bell from the Milany castle hermitage, and Plafalgàs shouldered it and set off back to the village.
claims.statement_id: Pastor paroki Sant Julià menugaskannya mengangkut lonceng dari pertapaan kastel Milany, dan Plafalgàs memikulnya di bahu pulang ke desa.
claims.quote: El rector de Sant Julià, que li encarregava feines diverses, li va encomanar la tasca de transportar la campana. Plafalgàs se la va carregar a l'espatlla i va emprendre el camí de tornada al poble.

claims.statement: The bell was so big that, when melted down, it made the four bells that hung in the parish tower until 1936.
claims.statement_id: Lonceng itu begitu besar sehingga setelah dilebur menjadi empat lonceng yang tergantung di menara gereja sampai 1936.
claims.quote: Per tenir idea de les dimensions de la campana, només cal saber que va ser fosa i en van sortir les quatre que, abans de l'any 1936, hi havia al campanar de la parròquia.

claims.statement: Teased by farmers, Plafalgàs bet that if they filled the bell with seven quarteres of grain and he carried it all to the village, the wheat would be his; leaning on a beech staff he carried bell and grain to Vallfogona.
claims.statement_id: Ditantang petani yang mengejeknya, Plafalgàs bertaruh bahwa bila lonceng itu diisi tujuh quartera gandum dan ia sanggup membawanya ke desa, gandum itu menjadi miliknya; dengan bantuan sebatang kayu beech ia membawa lonceng dan gandum itu ke Vallfogona.
claims.quote: Plafalgàs els va desafiar a que, si li omplien la campana amb set quarteres de gra i ho transportava tot fins a la vila, es quedaria el blat. Acceptada la juguesca, valent-se d'un buscall de faig va anar fins a Vallfogona amb la campana i el gra.

claims.statement: Tradition says Plafalgàs is buried right before the threshold of the church of Sant Julià, under a slab carved with a bell.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi Plafalgàs dimakamkan tepat di depan ambang pintu gereja Sant Julià, di bawah batu nisan berukir lonceng.
claims.quote: Segons la tradició, Plafalgàs està enterrat just al davant del llindar de la porta de l'església de Sant Julià —on solia seure en una enorme pila de pedra—, sota una llosa on hi ha gravada una campana.

claims.statement: In 2009 the village honoured its legendary figure by having master Tavi Algueró build a festival giant over three metres tall.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2009 desa itu menghormati tokoh legendarisnya dengan memesan boneka raksasa pesta setinggi lebih dari tiga meter dari Tavi Algueró.
claims.quote: L'any 2009, el poble va retre homenatge al seu personatge llegendari fent construir al mestre Tavi Algueró un gegant de festa major de més de tres metres d'alçada

claims.statement: He is known for his goodness, courage and enormous strength, which he uses to help his neighbours.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikenal karena kebaikan, keberanian, dan kekuatan besarnya yang ia pakai untuk menolong tetangga.
claims.quote: Han är känd för sin godhet, sitt mod och sin enorma styrka, som han använder till att hjälpa sina grannar.

claims.statement: Portumno or Portunus was a sea god worshipped on the coasts of Italy, chiefly among the Etruscans and Romans.
claims.statement_id: Portumno atau Portunus adalah dewa laut yang dipuja di pesisir Italia, terutama oleh orang Etruria dan Romawi.
claims.quote: Portumno o Portuno era el nombre de un dios marino adorado en las costas de Italia, principalmente entre los etruscos y romanos.

claims.statement: He was identified with Palaemon or Melicertes and sometimes with Neptune; he presided over entrances, especially harbours, and so was shown holding a key.
claims.statement_id: Ia disamakan dengan Palaemon atau Melikertes dan kadang dengan Neptunus; ia menguasai pintu masuk, terutama pelabuhan, sehingga digambarkan menggenggam kunci.
claims.quote: Se le identificaba con Palemón o Melicertes y algunas veces con Neptuno. Presidía las entradas principalmente de los puertos y por eso se le representaba empuñando una llave.

claims.statement: He had a temple at the Tiber port where the festival called the Portumnalia was held every 17 August.
claims.statement_id: Di pelabuhan sungai Tiber ia punya kuil tempat perayaan Portumnalia diadakan setiap 17 Agustus.
claims.quote: en el puerto del Tíber tenía un templo en el cual el 17 de agosto de cada año se celebraban las fiestas llamadas Portumnalia.

claims.statement: This sea deity belongs to the mythology of ancient Italy and had a temple at the Tiber port.
claims.statement_id: Dewa laut ini termasuk mitologi Italia kuno dan punya kuil di pelabuhan Tiber.
claims.quote: Esta divindade mariña pertence á mitoloxía da antiga Italia e no porto do Tíber tiña un templo

claims.statement: Rahovart (or Rahouart) is a demon named in Collin de Plancy's Dictionnaire Infernal (1818), which cites Durzel's Renaissance book Moralité; he is a companion of Satan and little is known about him.
claims.statement_id: Rahovart (atau Rahouart) adalah iblis yang disebut dalam Dictionnaire Infernal karya Collin de Plancy (1818), yang merujuk Moralité karya Durzel dari masa Renaisans; ia pendamping Setan dan hanya sedikit yang diketahui tentangnya.
claims.quote: Rahovart (or Rahouart) is a demon identified in Collin de Plancy's Dictionnaire Infernal (1818), according to which he is referenced in Durzel's Moralité, a Renaissance book. Rahovart is a companion of Satan; little is known about the demon himself.

claims.statement: Rahovart is assigned to torment the wicked, rich misers and old curmudgeons, and is also charged with avalanches and ghostly torment.
claims.statement_id: Rahovart bertugas menyiksa orang jahat, orang kaya yang kikir, dan orang tua pemarah, juga bertanggung jawab atas longsoran dan siksaan gaib.
claims.quote: Rahovart is attributed to the torment of evil, rich misers and old curmudgeons. He is also charged with avalanches and ghostly torment.

claims.statement: The elderly are reportedly most easily possessed by this demon, and if they die under its influence their souls go into Rahovart's basket until Judgement Day.
claims.statement_id: Orang tua konon paling mudah dirasuki iblis ini, dan bila mereka mati di bawah pengaruhnya, jiwa mereka dikumpulkan dalam keranjang Rahovart sampai hari kiamat.
claims.quote: Reportedly, the elderly are most easily subject to possession by this demon, and if the person should die under the demonic effect, their souls are collected into Rahovart's basket until the day of judgment.

claims.statement: Rahovart, or "Lord Rahovart", is a demon and companion of Satan mentioned in Durzel's Moralité, a Renaissance book printed in Rouen.
claims.statement_id: Rahovart atau "Tuan Rahovart" adalah iblis pendamping Setan yang disebut dalam Moralité karya Durzel, buku Renaisans yang dicetak di Rouen.
claims.quote: Rahovart, ou "Senhor Rahovart", é um demônio e companheiro de Satanás. Ele é referenciado no Moralidade de Durzel, um livro do Renascimento impresso em Rouen.

claims.statement: Ryangombe is a demigod, warrior and chief admired in life, who after death became leader of the Imandwa, a group of spirits mediating between Imana and humans.
claims.statement_id: Ryangombe adalah setengah dewa, pejuang, dan pemimpin yang dikagumi semasa hidupnya, yang setelah wafat menjadi pemimpin Imandwa, kelompok roh perantara antara Imana dan manusia.
claims.quote: Ryangombe est un demi-dieu, guerrier et chef, admiré de son vivant, qui, après sa mort, devint le chef des Imandwa, un groupe d’esprits qui servent d’intermédiaires entre Imana et les humains.

claims.statement: He came to Rwanda from western Uganda, from the district of Murilo Kitara.
claims.statement_id: Ia datang ke Rwanda dari Uganda barat, dari distrik Murilo Kitara.
claims.quote: Il est venu au Rwanda depuis l'ouest de l'Ouganda, dans le district de Murilo Kitara .

claims.statement: He first appeared in Rwanda under King Ruganzu II Ndoli around 1510, when he came to spread his religion.
claims.statement_id: Ia pertama kali muncul di Rwanda pada masa raja Ruganzu II Ndoli sekitar 1510, ketika datang untuk menyebarkan agamanya.
claims.quote: Il est apparu pour la première fois au Rwanda sous le règne du roi Ruganzu II Ndoli vers 1510, lorsqu'il est venu au Rwanda pour diffuser sa religion.

claims.statement: Ryangombe's father was Babinga wa Nyundo, his mother Nyiraryangombe wa Umusumbakazi and his wife Nyirakajumba.
claims.statement_id: Ayah Ryangombe bernama Babinga wa Nyundo, ibunya Nyiraryangombe wa Umusumbakazi, dan istrinya Nyirakajumba.
claims.quote: Le père de Ryangombe s'appelait Babinga wa Nyundo, sa mère s'appelait Nyiraryangombe wa Umusumbakazi et sa femme s'appelait Nyirakajumba.

claims.statement: Ryangombe was an only child and had five children: Binego, Ruhanga, Nyabirungu, Mashira and Kagoro.
claims.statement_id: Ryangombe anak tunggal dan punya lima anak: Binego, Ruhanga, Nyabirungu, Mashira, dan Kagoro.
claims.quote: Ryangombe est un enfant unique. Il eut lui-même cinq enfants : Binego, Ruhanga, Nyabirungu, Mashira et Kagoro.

claims.statement: According to the Kinyarwanda article, he is best known as the origin of the kubandwa and guterekera rites, which did not exist before his death.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Kinyarwanda, ia paling dikenal sebagai asal-usul ritual kubandwa dan guterekera, yang belum ada sebelum ia wafat.
claims.quote: Icyo azwiho cyane ni uko yabaye inkomoko yo kubandwa no guterekera kuko mbere yo gupfa kwe bitabagaho

claims.statement: The tac (Gascon lo tac) is a fantastic being of the legends and tales of Gascony, especially the Landes department.
claims.statement_id: Tac (bahasa Gascon: lo tac) adalah makhluk khayalan dalam legenda dan dongeng Gascogne, terutama departemen Landes.
claims.quote: Le tac (en gascon lo tac) est un être fantastique appartenant aux légendes et contes de la Gascogne et particulièrement du département des Landes.

claims.statement: The word's origin is unknown; it is related to the drac found throughout Occitania and close to the lébérou (Périgord) and the ganipote (Gironde, Charentes, Poitou).
claims.statement_id: Asal katanya tidak diketahui; ia berkerabat dengan drac yang dikenal di seluruh Occitania, dan mirip lébérou (Périgord) dan ganipote (Gironde, Charentes, Poitou).
claims.quote: L'origine du mot reste inconnue. Il est apparenté au drac qu'on retrouve dans toute l'Occitanie. Il se rapproche du lébérou (Périgord) et de la ganipote (Gironde, Charentes, Poitou).

claims.statement: It can take various forms, a basket, a lamb, a kid, and sometimes a horse that throws itself into a river, drowning those unlucky enough to ride it.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat berubah wujud menjadi keranjang, anak domba, atau anak kambing, dan kadang menjadi kuda yang terjun ke sungai sehingga penunggangnya tenggelam.
claims.quote: Il est capable de prendre différentes formes : panier, agneau, chevreau. Il peut également prendre parfois la forme d'un cheval, entraînant ainsi, en se jetant dans une rivière, la noyade de ceux qui ont le malheur de le monter.

claims.statement: The only form forbidden to it is a bridge, because that would kill too many victims.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya wujud yang terlarang baginya adalah jembatan, karena akan menewaskan terlalu banyak korban.
claims.quote: La seule forme qui lui est interdite est celle d'un pont car il entraînerait la mort d'un nombre trop important de victimes.

claims.statement: It appears at night in the woods or near the springs of the Landes, whistling like the hapchot, the tool of the Landes resin tapper.
claims.statement_id: Ia muncul pada malam hari di hutan atau dekat mata air Landes dan bersiul meniru bunyi hapchot, alat penyadap getah pinus Landes.
claims.quote: Il se manifeste la nuit dans les bois ou près des fontaines des Landes. Il peut alors siffler quand quelqu'un vient en imitant le bruit du hapchot, outil du gemmeur landais.

claims.statement: It always tries to get carried on a passer-by's back until the victim is exhausted and sometimes dies.
claims.statement_id: Ia selalu berusaha digendong di punggung orang yang lewat sampai korbannya kelelahan dan kadang mati.
claims.quote: Il cherche toujours  à se faire porter sur le dos de la personne qui passe et ceci jusqu'à l'épuisement et parfois le trépas de sa victime.

claims.statement: It is a mischievous being that tricks humans and laughs at their gullibility.
claims.statement_id: Ia makhluk usil yang menipu manusia dan menertawakan kepolosan mereka.
claims.quote: És una mena d'ésser entremaliat que enganya els humans i se'n riu de la seva credulitat

claims.statement: In Polynesian mythology, stories of Tinirau are found throughout the islands of Polynesia; he is a guardian of fish.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Polinesia, kisah tentang Tinirau ditemukan di seluruh kepulauan Polinesia; ia penjaga ikan.
claims.quote: In Polynesian mythology, stories about Tinirau are found throughout the islands of Polynesia. He is a guardian of fish.

claims.statement: Often he travels abroad to seek his wife or she seeks him; sometimes he mistreats her or she rejects him; he guards the fish, but it is his wife who gives each fish its characteristics.
claims.statement_id: Sering ia pergi ke negeri lain mencari istrinya, atau istrinya mencarinya; kadang ia memperlakukan istrinya dengan buruk atau ditolak; ia penjaga ikan, tetapi istrinyalah yang memberi tiap ikan ciri khasnya.
claims.quote: Often he travels to another land in search of his wife, or his wife travels to another land in search of him; sometimes he treats his wife badly, or she rejects him; while he is guardian of fish, it is his wife who gives the fish their individual characteristics.

claims.statement: In some traditions he has a dual nature, destructive as guardian of sharks and a kind, handsome youth; in others his right side is human and his left a fish.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian tradisi ia berwatak ganda, sisi perusak sebagai penjaga hiu dan sisi pemuda tampan yang baik; dalam tradisi lain sisi kanannya manusia dan sisi kirinya ikan.
claims.quote: In some traditions, he has a dual nature; one destructive as the guardian of sharks, and one a kind, handsome male youth; in others, his right side is human and his left side is a fish.

claims.statement: Other names in various Polynesian languages include Kinilau, Sinilau, Tigilau and Tinilau.
claims.statement_id: Nama lainnya dalam berbagai bahasa Polinesia antara lain Kinilau, Sinilau, Tigilau, dan Tinilau.
claims.quote: Alternate names in the various Polynesian languages include Kinilau, Sinilau, Tigilau, and Tinilau.

claims.statement: In a Samoan tale Tinilau lends his two turtles to ‘Ae of Tonga, who kills them for a great feast for his people.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Samoa, Tinilau meminjamkan dua penyunya kepada ‘Ae dari Tonga, yang membunuh penyu-penyu itu untuk pesta bagi rakyatnya.
claims.quote: Tinilau lends his two turtles to ‘Ae, a Tongan. When he gets home, ‘Ae kills the turtles and has a great feast for his people.

claims.statement: When a bloody wave washes ashore, Tinilau summons the avenging gods of Savaii, who seize ‘Ae from Tonga and bring him to Tinilau's house.
claims.statement_id: Ketika ombak berdarah sampai ke pantai, Tinilau mengumpulkan dewa-dewa pembalas dari Savaii yang lalu menculik ‘Ae dari Tonga dan membawanya ke rumah Tinilau.
claims.quote: When a bloody wave washes up on the beach, Tinilau calls a meeting of all the avenging gods of Savaii. The gods go to Tonga and pick 'Ae up, and return him to the house of Tinilau.

claims.statement: One day while Tigilau is fishing, a jealous wife steals Sina's soul, and Tigilau travels to the sun to get it back.
claims.statement_id: Suatu hari saat Tigilau memancing, salah satu istrinya yang cemburu mencuri jiwa Sina, dan Tigilau pergi ke matahari untuk mengambilnya kembali.
claims.quote: One day, Tigilau goes out fishing, and one of the jealous wives steals Sina's soul. To get it back, Tigilau travels to the sun

claims.statement: Tinilau or Tinirau is a Polynesian god, guardian of fish, in the culture of Samoa and Hawaii and in the Māori mythology of New Zealand and the Cook Islands.
claims.statement_id: Tinilau atau Tinirau adalah dewa Polinesia penjaga ikan dalam budaya Samoa, Hawaii, dan mitologi Maori Selandia Baru serta Kepulauan Cook.
claims.quote: Tinilau ou Tinirau est un dieu polynésien gardien des poissons, dans la culture de l'île de Samoa, de Hawaï ou dans la mythologie maorie de Nouvelle-Zélande et des Îles Cook.

claims.statement: Today the cult of the "Lord of the four directions of Tlalocan" is still alive, its festival gathering the nine barrios of the area.
claims.statement_id: Kini pemujaan "Tuan dari empat penjuru Tlalocan" masih hidup, dan perayaannya mengumpulkan sembilan kampung di wilayah itu.
claims.quote: En la actualidad, el culto al “Señor de los cuatro rumbos del Tlalocan”, se mantiene vigente, su festividad congrega a los nueve barrios que conforman su actual geografía política

claims.statement: In Aztec mythology he is a helper of Tlaloc, one of the four tlaloque responsible for distributing rain on earth.

claims.quote: в ацтекській міфології, помічник Тлалока; один із чотирьох тлалоке, відповідальних за розподіл дощу на землі.

claims.statement: His name is linked to the mountain of the same name near lakes Chalco and Xochimilco.
claims.statement_id: Namanya terkait dengan gunung bernama sama di dekat danau Chalco dan Xochimilco.
claims.quote: Його ім'я пов'язане із однойменною горою, поблизу озер Халко та Сохімілько.

claims.statement: Sardinian folk legends tell of the Scultone, a reptile-like, dragon-like animal that killed people and animals; near Baunei the dragon's flight is said to have opened the Golgo chasm.
claims.statement_id: Legenda rakyat Sardinia menyebut Scultone, hewan mirip reptil seperti naga yang membunuh manusia dan hewan; di dekat Baunei, kaburnya naga ini konon membuka jurang Golgo.
claims.quote: Le leggende folcloristiche sarde riferiscono dell'esistenza dello Scultone, un animale rettiliforme simile ad un drago che uccideva uomini e animali: presso Baunei (NU), la fuga di un drago chiamato Scultone avrebbe aperto la voragine del Golgo.

claims.statement: Because the Scultone's gaze could kill, the apostle Peter looked at it through a small mirror, neutralising that power and sinking the dragon into the bowels of the earth.
claims.statement_id: Karena tatapan Scultone dapat membunuh, Rasul Petrus memandangnya lewat cermin kecil, sehingga kekuatan itu hilang dan naga itu tenggelam ke perut bumi.
claims.quote: poiché lo sguardo dello  Scultone aveva il potere di uccidere, Pietro lo avrebbe guardato per mezzo di un piccolo specchio, neutralizzando tale potere e facendo sprofondare il Drago nelle viscere della Terra.

claims.statement: The Scultone appears as a basilisk, the main antagonist of the Martin Mystère comic story "Il Mistero del Nuraghe".
claims.statement_id: Scultone muncul dalam wujud basilisk sebagai lawan utama di komik Martin Mystère kisah "Il Mistero del Nuraghe".
claims.quote: Lo Scultone compare sotto forma di Basilisco all'interno dei fumetti di Martin Mystère, come principale antagonista della storia "Il Mistero del Nuraghe"

claims.statement: In the Corsican version U Scultone is a reptile-like, dragon-like animal that killed people and animals, lived among the shrubs and was immortal.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Korsika, U Scultone adalah hewan mirip reptil seperti naga yang membunuh manusia dan hewan, hidup di semak-semak, dan abadi.
claims.quote: U Scultone ghjè un animale rettiliforme simile à un dracone chì uccidìa omi è animali, vivìa trà l'arbusti è era immortale.

claims.statement: The Valais Monster (Monstre du Valais), also called the Eischoll Wolf or the Mysterious Animal of Leuk, is the nickname of one or more ferocious beasts that attacked many herds in the canton of Valais, Switzerland, from April 1946.
claims.statement_id: Monster Valais (Monstre du Valais), disebut juga Serigala Eischoll atau Hewan Misterius Leuk, adalah julukan bagi satu atau beberapa binatang buas yang menyerang banyak ternak di kanton Valais, Swiss, sejak April 1946.
claims.quote: Valais Monster (French: Monstre du Valais), also known as Eischoll Wolf, and Mysterious animal of Leuk (French: Animal mystérieux de la Loèche), is the nickname of one or more ferocious beasts that attacked numerous herds in the canton of Valais, Switzerland, from April 1946.

claims.statement: Among many supposed identities, a lynx or one or more panthers dominated, but the monster seems to have been a large European wolf shot at Eischoll on 27 November 1947.
claims.statement_id: Di antara banyak dugaan, yang paling menonjol adalah lynx atau satu atau beberapa macan kumbang, tetapi monster itu tampaknya seekor serigala Eropa besar yang ditembak di Eischoll pada 27 November 1947.
claims.quote: Among a multitude of supposed identities, those of a lynx or one or several panthers dominate, supported by testimonies followed by many in the media. However, the Valais Monster seems to have been a large European wolf, shot in Eischoll on 27 November 1947.

claims.statement: The case shows the population's tendency to imagine dangerous big cats, based on fear and mistaken testimony.
claims.statement_id: Kasus ini menunjukkan kecenderungan penduduk membayangkan kehadiran kucing besar berbahaya berdasarkan rasa takut dan kesaksian keliru.
claims.quote: It testifies to the tendency of the population to imagine the presence of dangerous felines, based on fear and erroneous testimonies.

claims.statement: According to Alexandre Scheurer, the people of Valais have a "perception of fauna dominated by fear and fantasy".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Alexandre Scheurer, penduduk Valais memandang satwa liar dengan "persepsi yang dikuasai rasa takut dan khayalan".
claims.quote: According to Alexandre Scheurer, the inhabitants of Valais have a "perception of fauna dominated by fear and fantasy".

claims.statement: In 1966 S. Corinna Bille published a book, Le Mystère du Monstre, about the whole affair.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1966 S. Corinna Bille menerbitkan buku Le Mystère du Monstre tentang seluruh peristiwa ini.
claims.quote: In 1966, S. Corinna Bille published a book entitled Le Mystère du Monstre (The Mystery of the Monster), which referred to the whole affair.

claims.statement: The Swiss press called it a "monster".
claims.statement_id: Pers Swiss memakai sebutan "monster" untuknya.
claims.quote: La presse suisse utilise le nom de « monstre ».

claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Yunani, Aite (Aithe) adalah nama salah satu kuda Agamemnon; yang lain bernama Podargos.
claims.quote: Nella mitologia greca, Aite era il nome di uno dei cavalli di Agamennone; l'altro si chiamava Podargo.

claims.statement: Echepolus gave the two horses to Agamemnon as compensation for not joining his war expedition to Troy.
claims.statement_id: Echepolos menghadiahkan kedua kuda itu kepada Agamemnon sebagai ganti karena tidak ikut dalam ekspedisi perang ke Troya.
claims.quote: Echepolo aveva donato i due cavalli ad Agamennone, grande re della Grecia, come risarcimento per non averlo potuto seguire nella sua spedizione bellica a Troia.

claims.statement: Aite was the mare of the pair, with a beautiful mane and swift in the race.
claims.statement_id: Aite adalah kuda betina dari pasangan itu, bersurai indah dan cepat berlari.
claims.quote: Aite era il cavallo femmina della coppia, aveva una bella criniera ed era veloce nella corsa.

claims.statement: The horses ran in the funeral games for Patroclus, friend of Achilles; in the race, driven by Menelaus, Aite nearly overtook Antilochus.
claims.statement_id: Kuda-kuda itu ikut dalam pertandingan pemakaman untuk menghormati Patroklos, sahabat Akhilleus; dalam balapan yang dikemudikan Menelaos, Aite nyaris menyusul Antilokhos.
claims.quote: I cavalli parteciparono ai giochi funebri tenuti per onorare la morte di Patroclo, grande amico dell'invincibile Achille. Durante la corsa, guidata dal fratello del proprietario, Menelao, Aite per poco non riuscì a superare Antiloco.

claims.statement: According to the Greek article, Aithe was the reddish-blonde mare that King Echepolus of Sicyon gave to Agamemnon.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Yunani, Aithe adalah kuda betina berwarna pirang kemerahan yang dihadiahkan raja Sikyon, Echepolos, kepada Agamemnon.
claims.quote: Στην ελληνική μυθολογία Αίθη ήταν το όνομα της κοκκινόξανθης φοράδας που χάρισε ο βασιλέας της Σικυώνας Εχέπωλος στον Αγαμέμνονα

claims.statement: Wollunqua, also written Wollunka or Wollunkua, is a snake god of rain and fertility in the Aboriginal mythology of the Warramunga people of Australia's Northern Territory, a variant of the "Rainbow Serpent" known to many other Aboriginal peoples.
claims.statement_id: Wollunqua, juga ditulis Wollunka atau Wollunkua, adalah dewa ular hujan dan kesuburan dalam mitologi Aborigin suku Warramunga di Northern Territory, Australia, sebuah variasi "Ular Pelangi" yang dikenal banyak suku Aborigin lain.
claims.quote: Wollunqua, also written Wollunka or Wollunkua, is a snake-god of rain and fertility in Australian Aboriginal mythology of the Warramunga people of the Northern Territory of Australia, a variation of the "Rainbow Serpent" present in the mythology of many other Aboriginal Australian peoples.

claims.statement: The snake, which emerged from a waterhole called Kadjinara in the Murchison Ranges, is said to be many miles long.
claims.statement_id: Ular itu muncul dari lubang air bernama Kadjinara di Pegunungan Murchison dan konon panjangnya bermil-mil.
claims.quote: The snake, which emerged from a watering hole called Kadjinara in the Murchison Ranges, is said to be many miles long.

claims.statement: In public the snake is called urkulu nappaurinnia, because calling its real name too often would make it break loose, come out and devour everyone; it can place the rainbow in the sky at will.
claims.statement_id: Di depan umum ular ini disebut urkulu nappaurinnia, karena bila nama aslinya terlalu sering disebut ia akan lepas kendali, keluar, dan melahap semua orang; ia dapat menaruh pelangi di langit sesuka hati.
claims.quote: When speaking of the Wollunqua snake in public, the name urkulu nappaurinnia is used, because if they were to call it too often by its real name they would lose control and it would come out and devour them all. It can place the rainbow in the sky at will.

claims.statement: Wollunqua is a totemic ancestor of the Warramunga, specifically the tribe's Uluuru moiety.
claims.statement_id: Wollunqua adalah leluhur totem suku Warramunga, khususnya paruh Uluuru suku itu.
claims.quote: Wollunqua is a totemic ancestor of the Warramunga people, specifically the Uluuru moiety of the tribe.

claims.statement: Heading east, he first travelled underground, surfacing at various spots to perform ceremonies and leaving many spirit children that became local totemic centres.
claims.statement_id: Dalam perjalanannya ke timur ia mula-mula bergerak di bawah tanah, muncul di berbagai tempat untuk melakukan upacara dan meninggalkan banyak anak roh yang menjadi pusat totem setempat.
claims.quote: Setting out towards the east, he travelled at first underground, coming up at various spots where he performed ceremonies and left behind large numbers of spirit children, forming local totemic centres when he passed on.

claims.statement: He was so long that though his head had travelled many miles from Kadjinara, his tail was still there.
claims.statement_id: Ia begitu panjang sehingga meski kepalanya sudah bermil-mil dari Kadjinara, ekornya masih berada di sana.
claims.quote: for he was so long that although he had travelled very many miles away from his home at Kadjinara, his tail end still remained there.

claims.statement: In Aboriginal mythology Wollunqua is a snake god of rain and fertility of the Warumungu people in Australia's Northern Territory.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Aborigin, Wollunqua adalah dewa ular hujan dan kesuburan suku Warumungu di Northern Territory, Australia.
claims.quote: Dans la mythologie aborigène, Wollunqua (encore écrit Wollunka ou Wollunkua) est un dieu-serpent de la pluie et de la fertilité du peuple Warumungu dans le Territoire du Nord, en Australie.

claims.statement: In Acaxochitlán, Yauhqueme is the tlaloque of the west, owner of yellow maize, now revered as the Christ of Huayotenco, "Señor de Tlacpac".
claims.statement_id: Di Acaxochitlán, Yauhqueme adalah tlaloque arah barat, pemilik jagung kuning, yang kini dihormati sebagai Kristus dari Huayotenco, "Señor de Tlacpac".
claims.quote: Y al oeste, Yauhqueme (el vestido de Yauhtli o pericón), en veneración del tlaloque dueño del maíz amarillo, resignificado en la figura del Cristo de Huayotenco o “señor del buen camino”, como “Señor de Tlacpac”.

claims.statement: In Aztec mythology he is a helper of Tlaloc, one of the four tlaloque who distribute rain on earth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Aztek ia pembantu Tlaloc, salah satu dari empat tlaloque yang membagikan hujan di bumi.

claims.statement: His name is linked to a hill of the same name near Atlacuihuayan (now Tacubaya), where children were sacrificed to the rain gods; he was also a deity of the Otomi.
claims.statement_id: Namanya terkait dengan bukit bernama sama dekat Atlacuihuayan (kini Tacubaya), tempat anak-anak dikorbankan bagi dewa-dewa hujan; ia juga dewa orang Otomi.
claims.quote: Його ім'я пов'язане з однойменним пагорбом поблизу Атлакуїхуая (теперішня Такубая), де богам дощу приносили в жертву дітей. Був також божеством Отомі.

claims.statement: His attire was a paper hat, a feather train, a paper strip on the chest and sandals; in one hand he held a rattle and in the other a shield.
claims.statement_id: Pakaiannya terdiri atas topi kertas, juntaian bulu, pita kertas di dada, dan sandal; satu tangannya memegang kerincingan dan tangan lainnya perisai.
claims.quote: Його одяг складався з паперового капелюха, шлейфа із пір'я, смужки паперу на грудях, сандалів. Однією рукою він тримав брязкальце, а іншою — щит.

claims.statement: In Basque mythology Zezengorri ('red bull', from zezen 'bull' and gorri 'red') is a spirit living in caves or underground cavities that takes the form of a red bull when it comes out.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Basque, Zezengorri ("banteng merah", dari zezen "banteng" dan gorri "merah") adalah roh yang tinggal di gua atau rongga bawah tanah dan berwujud banteng merah saat keluar.
claims.quote: En la mitologia basca, Zezengorri ('toro vermell', del basc zezen 'toro' i gorri 'vermell') és un geni que viu en coves o altres cavitats subterrànies i que, en sortir-ne, adopta la forma de toro vermell.

claims.statement: In some areas or legends it is a red cow instead, called Behigorri.
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa daerah ia berupa sapi betina merah dan disebut Behigorri.
claims.quote: Segons la zona o la llegenda, en comptes d'un toro és una vaca vermella i aleshores se l'anomena Behigorri (behi és 'vaca' en basc).

claims.statement: The cave bulls of Basque mythology are mostly aggressive and may attack and frighten people in the cave or refuse them entry.
claims.statement_id: Banteng-banteng gua dalam mitologi Basque umumnya agresif, dapat menyerang dan menakuti orang di gua atau melarang mereka masuk.
claims.quote: Les taureaux cavernicoles de la mythologie basque sont pour la plupart agressifs et peuvent attaquer et effrayer les gens dans la grotte ou leur refuser l'entrée.

claims.statement: A fire bull (or gold, in some versions) lives in the cave of Austokieta on Mount Oxabi (Lizartza) and guards the caves of Mari.
claims.statement_id: Seekor banteng api (atau emas) tinggal di gua Austokieta di gunung Oxabi, Lizartza, dan menjaga gua-gua Mari.
claims.quote: Un toro de foc (o d'or, segons les variants) habita la cova d'Austokieta, a la muntanya d'Oxabi (Lizartza) i és el guardià de les coves de Mari.

claims.statement: A red bull breathing fire from its mouth and muzzle guards a treasure in the cave of Atxulaur near Orozko.
claims.statement_id: Seekor banteng merah yang menyemburkan api dari mulut dan moncongnya menjaga harta di gua Atxulaur dekat Orozko.
claims.quote: Un toro vermell que treu foc per la boca i el musell guarda un tresor a la cova d'Atxulaur (prop d'Orozko ).

claims.statement: Recent studies show that Zezengorri, Behigorri, Aatxe and other beings are linked to places where Palaeolithic people depicted those same animals.
claims.statement_id: Penelitian baru menunjukkan Zezengorri, Behigorri, Aatxe, dan makhluk lain dikaitkan dengan tempat-tempat yang memiliki gambar hewan yang sama dari manusia Paleolitik.
claims.quote: Estudis recents han demostrat que tant Zezengorri, Behigorri i Aatxe com altres entitats mitològiques (Ihizi, els laminak), s'associen amb llocs on aquests mateixos animals van ser representats pels homes del Paleolític.

claims.quote: Nella mitologia greca,  Abaste  era il nome di uno dei cavalli di Ade.

claims.statement: According to some mythographers Abaste was one of the man-eating horses of Diomedes.

claims.quote: Abhartach (pronounced [ˈəuɾˠt̪ˠəx]; Irish for 'dwarf'), also Avartagh, is an early Irish legend, which was first collected in Patrick Weston Joyce's The Origin and History of Irish Names of Places (1870).

claims.statement: The central figure strikingly resembles later ideas of vampires, and some 21st-century scholars suggest the legend may have inspired Bram Stoker's Dracula.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh utamanya sangat mirip gagasan vampir di kemudian hari, dan sebagian sarjana abad ke-21 menduga legenda ini mengilhami Bram Stoker menciptakan Dracula.

claims.statement: The dwarf was a magician and dreadful tyrant who, after great cruelties, was finally defeated and slain by a neighbouring chieftain, some say by Fionn Mac Cumhail.
claims.statement_id: Kerdil ini penyihir dan tiran mengerikan yang setelah berbuat sangat kejam akhirnya dikalahkan dan dibunuh kepala suku tetangga, menurut sebagian orang oleh Fionn Mac Cumhail.
claims.quote: This dwarf was a magician, and a dreadful tyrant, and after having perpetrated great cruelties on the people he was at last vanquished and slain by a neighbouring chieftain; some say by Fionn Mac Cumhail.

claims.statement: He was buried standing up, but the very next day appeared in his old haunts, crueller and stronger than ever.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikubur dalam posisi berdiri, tetapi keesokan harinya muncul lagi di tempat lamanya, lebih kejam dan kuat dari sebelumnya.
claims.quote: He was buried in a standing posture, but the very next day he appeared in his old haunts, more cruel and vigorous than ever.

claims.statement: After he escaped the grave again, the chief consulted a druid, slew him a third time and buried him head downwards, which subdued his magic so he never appeared again.
claims.statement_id: Setelah ia lolos lagi dari kubur, kepala suku berkonsultasi dengan seorang druid, membunuhnya untuk ketiga kalinya, dan menguburnya dengan kepala di bawah, sehingga kekuatan sihirnya padam dan ia tak pernah muncul lagi.
claims.quote: The chief then consulted a druid, and according to his directions, he slew the dwarf a third time, and buried him in the same place, with his head downwards; which subdued his magical power, so that he never again appeared on earth.

claims.statement: In some modern versions Abhartach rises from his grave to drink his subjects' blood, and the chieftain who slays him is named Cathain.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa versi modern Abhartach bangkit dari kubur untuk meminum darah rakyatnya, dan kepala suku yang membunuhnya bernama Cathain.
claims.quote: In some modern versions of the story Abhartach rises from his grave to drink the blood of his subjects, while the chieftain who slays the revenant is named as Cathain.

claims.statement: In those versions he can only be restrained by killing him with a yew-wood sword, burying him upside down, ringing the grave with thorns and placing a large stone on top.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi itu ia hanya dapat ditahan dengan dibunuh memakai pedang kayu yew, dikubur terbalik, kuburnya dikelilingi duri, dan ditindih batu besar.
claims.quote: he can only be restrained by killing him with a sword made of yew wood, burying him upside down, surrounding his grave with thorns, and placing a large stone on top of the grave.

claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi nelayan dan pelaut Portugal, alma de mestre adalah arwah nakhoda atau kapten kapal yang tewas dalam kapal karam.
claims.quote: Uma alma de mestre é, nas tradições dos pescadores e marinheiros de Portugal, a alma de um mestre ou capitão de um navio que se perdeu em naufrágio.

claims.statement: The belief comes from the plaintive cries of certain birds, above all the storm petrel (Hydrobates pelagicus), which sailors believe are the laments of the souls of masters and captains.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan ini berasal dari cicitan sedih burung tertentu, terutama petrel badai (Hydrobates pelagicus), yang diyakini pelaut sebagai ratapan arwah para nakhoda dan kapten.
claims.quote: A crença deve-se aos pios sentidos de certas aves, por antonomásia o Hydrobates pelagicus, que os marinheiros crêem serem os lamentos das almas dos mestres e capitães

claims.statement: They keep up their lament as long as their bodies have not reached land and received Christian burial.
claims.statement_id: Mereka terus meratap selama jasadnya belum sampai ke darat dan belum dimakamkan secara Kristen.

claims.statement: The Avurje (also Aure or Iura) is the figure of a popular belief widespread in the province of Taranto, especially Massafra and the old town of Taranto.
claims.statement_id: Avurje (juga Aure atau Iura) adalah tokoh kepercayaan rakyat yang tersebar luas di provinsi Taranto, terutama di Massafra dan kota tua Taranto.
claims.quote: L'Avurje (anche Aure o Iura) è il protagonista di una credenza popolare molto diffusa nella provincia di Taranto, in particolare a Massafra e nel borgo antico di Taranto.

claims.statement: It is a sprite or spirit that appears at night, especially towards dawn, in the form of a cat wearing a hat, settling on a sleeper's chest, paralysing them and taking their breath.
claims.statement_id: Ia peri atau roh yang muncul pada malam hari, terutama menjelang fajar, berwujud kucing bertopi, lalu duduk di dada orang tidur hingga lumpuh dan sesak napas.
claims.quote: Si tratta di un folletto o spirito che appare di notte, soprattutto verso l'alba, assumendo le sembianze di un gatto con un cappello, e si posa sul petto del malcapitato dormiente, paralizzandolo e togliendogli il respiro.

claims.statement: Roberto Caprara's dictionary of the Massafra dialect defines A(v)ùrje (from Latin augurium) as a sprite that roams houses at night and enjoys braiding sleeping girls' hair and horses' manes.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus dialek Massafra karya Roberto Caprara, A(v)ùrje (dari bahasa Latin augurium) adalah roh peri yang berkeliaran di rumah pada malam hari dan suka mengepang rambut gadis yang tidur dan surai kuda.
claims.quote: l'A(v)ùrje (s.m. lat. augurium) è definito uno spirito folletto che si aggira di notte per le case e si diverte a intrecciare i capelli delle ragazze nel sonno e le criniere dei cavalli.

claims.statement: Others trace the superstition to a folk interpretation of sleep paralysis.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang menganggap takhayul ini tafsir rakyat atas kelumpuhan tidur.
claims.quote: Altri, invece, riconducono la superstizione ad una interpretazione popolare della paralisi nel sonno.

claims.statement: Tradition says that whoever is quick enough to snatch the Avurie's hat will enslave it and can force it to reveal a hidden treasure.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi, siapa yang sigap merebut topi Avurie akan menjadikannya budak dan dapat memaksanya menunjukkan tempat harta tersembunyi.
claims.quote: La tradizione vuole che se si ha la prontezza di strappare il cappello all'Avurie, lo si renderà schiavo e lo si potrà costringere a rivelare il nascondiglio di un tesoro nascosto.

claims.statement: In other parts of the province it is thought to take the form of a dog or a dove.
claims.statement_id: Di daerah lain provinsi itu ia dianggap berwujud anjing atau merpati.
claims.quote: In altre zone della provincia si pensa abbia forma di cane o colombo.

claims.statement: An Aure may belong to a house and never leave it, or be tied to a family and follow it wherever it moves.
claims.statement_id: Aure bisa terikat pada sebuah rumah dan tak pernah meninggalkannya, atau pada sebuah keluarga dan mengikutinya ke mana pun mereka pindah.
claims.quote: L'Aure può essere proprio di un'abitazione, ed allora non l'abbandonerà mai, o essere legato ad una famiglia, ed allora la seguirà nei suoi spostamenti.

claims.statement: The Babau (also Babao, Bobò, Baubau, Mau Mau and others) is, in Italian and other European folklore, an imaginary monster of ill-defined features traditionally invoked to frighten children.
claims.statement_id: Babau (juga Babao, Bobò, Baubau, Mau Mau, dan lain-lain) dalam cerita rakyat Italia dan Eropa lain adalah monster khayalan berwujud tidak jelas yang biasa disebut untuk menakuti anak-anak.
claims.quote: Il Babau (più raramente Babao, Bobò, Barabao, Maramao, Baubau, Bau Bau, Mamau, Maumau o Mau Mau) è, nel folclore italiano e in altri folclori europei, un mostro immaginario dalle caratteristiche non ben definite che viene tradizionalmente evocato per spaventare i bambini

claims.statement: The Babau is closely related to the uomo nero and the ogre of fairy tales, and the names can even be used interchangeably.
claims.statement_id: Babau sangat berkaitan dengan uomo nero ("lelaki hitam") dan orc dalam dongeng, bahkan nama-nama itu bisa dipakai bergantian.
claims.quote: Si può intendere il Babau come strettamente correlato all'uomo nero e all'orco delle fiabe, o addirittura usare queste diverse denominazioni come sinonimi.

claims.statement: Some sources say the Babau may be a legacy of the old fear of the Saracens (9th–10th centuries), its name perhaps from Arabic Baban, "victor".
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian sumber, Babau mungkin warisan ketakutan lama terhadap orang Saracen (abad ke-9 sampai ke-10), dan namanya mungkin berasal dari kata Arab Baban, "pemenang".
claims.quote: Secondo alcune fonti, il Babau potrebbe essere un retaggio dell'antico timore nei confronti dei Saraceni (IX-X secolo). In questo caso, la parola "Babau" potrebbe derivare dall'arabo Baban (ossia "Vincitore").

claims.statement: A more common view takes the name as onomatopoeic, a doubling of a dog's bark or another animal's cry.
claims.statement_id: Tafsir yang lebih umum menganggap Babau tiruan bunyi, dari pengulangan gonggongan anjing atau suara hewan lain.
claims.quote: Un'interpretazione più diffusa intende invece il nome "Babau" come onomatopea, ottenuto per raddoppiamento dal latrato del cane o di un altro animale.

claims.statement: Dino Buzzati wrote a short story titled after the Babau and also painted it several times.
claims.statement_id: Dino Buzzati menulis cerita pendek berjudul Babau dan juga melukisnya dalam beberapa lukisan.
claims.quote: Al Babau è dedicato il racconto omonimo di Dino Buzzati (che lo ritrasse anche in diversi dipinti).

claims.quote: Il badalischio è una tipica leggenda della valle del Casentino (Toscana, Provincia di Arezzo).

claims.statement: This monster, similar to the basilisk, is said to have been born in the Gorga Nera, a small lake near the Fonte del Borbotto in the Casentino Forests National Park.

claims.statement: It is a strange serpent as big as a man, wrapped in linen swaddling bands, with red eyes able to paralyse its prey.
claims.statement_id: Ia ular aneh sebesar manusia, terbungkus kain lampin linen bayi, dengan mata merah yang dapat melumpuhkan mangsanya.
claims.quote: uno strano serpente, grande come un uomo, avvolto in bende di lino da neonato, con occhi rossi in grado di paralizzare la malcapitata preda.

claims.statement: Some legends say its breath is extremely poisonous, even deadly, and it is often shown with a crown or diadem that sometimes covers its eyes.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian legenda menyebut napasnya sangat beracun bahkan mematikan, dan ia sering digambarkan bermahkota atau berdiadem yang kadang menutupi matanya.
claims.quote: Alcune leggende affermano che l'alito del badalischio sia estremamente velenoso, addirittura mortale. Il badalischio viene spesso raffigurato con una corona od un diadema, che a volte gli copre gli occhi.

claims.statement: The balborinho (also borborinho, barborinho or belborinho) is a mythical being of Portuguese folklore, a whirlwind that appears at the "open hours", mainly at crossroads.
claims.statement_id: Balborinho (juga borborinho, barborinho, atau belborinho) adalah makhluk mitos cerita rakyat Portugal, pusaran angin yang muncul pada "jam terbuka", terutama di persimpangan jalan.
claims.quote: O balborinho (grafias alternativas borborinho, barborinho ou belborinho) é um ser mítico do folclore português. O balborinho é um redemoinho de vento que surge nas horas abertas, principalmente nas encruzilhadas dos caminhos.

claims.statement: Inside the balborinho travel the lost souls of peasants who committed agrarian crimes and cannot enter heaven because they owe the living and must return what they stole.
claims.statement_id: Di dalam balborinho berputar arwah gentayangan petani yang melakukan kejahatan atas tanah dan tidak bisa masuk surga karena masih berutang kepada orang hidup dan harus mengembalikan apa yang mereka curi.
claims.quote: Dentro do balborinho vão as almas penadas de campesinos que cometeram delitos agrários, e não podem entrar no céu por estarem em dívida para com os vivos, tendo necessidade de lhes restituir o que surripiaram.

claims.statement: In the 19th century, many parts of the country believed devils and witches appeared within the balborinhos.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-19, di berbagai daerah orang percaya bahwa di dalam balborinho muncul iblis dan penyihir.
claims.quote: Em várias zonas do país, no século XIX, havia a crença de que no seio dos balborinhos surgem diabos e bruxas.

claims.statement: In Briteiros people crossed themselves while saying, "Go to whoever ate your fields".
claims.statement_id: Di Briteiros orang membuat tanda salib sambil berkata "Pergilah kepada orang yang memakan ladangmu".
claims.quote: Em Briteiros, a recomendação que se fazia era persignar-se, enquanto se lhes dizia a seguinte invocação: «Vai-te para quem te comeu as leiras».

claims.statement: In Moncorvo people threw an open penknife into the centre of the whirlwind to drive out the witch hiding inside.
claims.statement_id: Di Moncorvo orang melemparkan pisau lipat terbuka ke tengah pusaran untuk mengusir penyihir yang bersembunyi di dalamnya.
claims.quote: Em Moncorvo, por sua vez, recomendava-se atirar um canivete aberto ao centro do redemoinho de vento, a fim de esmadrigar de dentro do balborinho a Feiticeira ou Bruxa, que nele se ocultava.

claims.statement: In Guimarães it was believed a devil rode on every leaf the balborinho's wind snatched up.
claims.statement_id: Di Guimarães orang percaya setiap daun yang terbawa angin balborinho membawa seorang iblis.
claims.quote: Em Guimarães era crendice popular que em cada folha arrebatada ao vento de um balborinho ia um diabo.

claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Katalan, baldemora adalah semacam putri duyung berambut panjang, kadang keemasan kadang keperakan, yang bergerak sangat cepat; ia tinggal di laut dan membantu memandu pelaut yang tersesat karena laut buruk.
claims.quote: Una baldemora és, dins la mitologia catalana, una mena de sirena amb una llarga cabellera, a voltes daurada, a voltes platejada que es mou amb gran rapidesa. Viu dins de la mar i ajuda a guiar els mariners quan aquests han perdut el nord per culpa de la mala maror.

claims.statement: Because it holds its feast on Saint Peter's day, it is best not to go to sea that day, since the baldemora will not watch over the ships.
claims.statement_id: Karena ia merayakan pestanya pada hari Santo Petrus, pada hari itu sebaiknya tidak melaut, sebab baldemora tidak akan menjaga perjalanan kapal.
claims.quote: Com que celebra la seva festa per Sant Pere, aquest dia el millor és no fer-se a la mar, perquè la baldemora no vetllarà per la bona marxa de les naus.

claims.statement: Banya Verda ("green horn") is a child-scaring bogey of Catalan folk imagination, a devil with a big green horn in the middle of its forehead that pricks naughty children with a pitchfork, loads them in a basket and takes them straight to hell.
claims.statement_id: Banya Verda ("tanduk hijau") adalah momok penakut anak imajinasi rakyat Katalan, iblis bertanduk hijau besar di tengah dahi yang menusuk anak nakal dengan garpu tala, memasukkan mereka ke keranjang, dan membawa mereka langsung ke neraka.
claims.quote: En Banya Verda és un espantamainades propi de l'imaginari popular català. Es tracta d'un dimoni que té una gran banya verda al mig del front. Duu una forca amb què punxa tots els nens dolents que troba, se'ls carrega en una cistella i se'ls enduu de pet a l'infern.

claims.statement: The figure is especially known in the Cerdanya, but also in Mallorca, where it is one of the protagonists of the traditional cossiers dances of Montuïri.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh ini terkenal terutama di Cerdanya, tetapi juga di Mallorca, tempat ia menjadi salah satu tokoh tarian tradisional cossiers di Montuïri.
claims.quote: El personatge és especialment conegut a la Cerdanya, però també a Mallorca, on és un dels protagonistes dels balls tradicionals dels cossiers de Montuïri.

claims.statement: The Banyoles monster is a legendary monster, possibly a dragon, from the lake of Banyoles in Catalonia.
claims.statement_id: Monster Banyoles adalah monster legendaris, mungkin seekor naga, dari danau Banyoles di Katalonia.
claims.quote: The Banyoles monster is a legendary monster, possibly a dragon, from the Lake of Banyoles in Catalonia.

claims.statement: In the 8th century a French monk named St Emeterio coaxed the beast from the lake with prayers and turned it into a peaceful herbivore; it is said to live in the depths of the lake still.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-8, seorang biarawan Prancis bernama Santo Emeterio membujuk binatang itu keluar dari danau dengan doa dan mengubahnya menjadi pemakan tumbuhan yang damai; konon ia masih hidup di dasar danau sampai kini.
claims.quote: In the eighth century, a French monk named St. Emeterio coaxed the beast from the lake using prayers and transformed the creature into a peaceful herbivore. It is said the Banyoles Monster still lives in the depth of the lake today.

claims.statement: The monster is the subject of the 2008 children's song "El Monstre De Banyoles" by Toni Jiménez.
claims.statement_id: Monster ini menjadi subjek lagu anak "El Monstre De Banyoles" karya Toni Jiménez tahun 2008.
claims.quote: The monster is the subject of a 2008 children's song "El Monstre De Banyoles" by Toni Jiménez.

claims.statement: According to the Catalan article on the Drac de Banyoles, the huge, fierce dragon had its lair in the lake of Banyoles, in the cave of La Draga.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Katalan tentang Drac de Banyoles, naga yang besar dan buas itu bersarang di danau Banyoles, di gua La Draga.
claims.quote: el drac, enorme i ferotge, tenia el cau a l'estany de Banyoles, concretament, a la cova de la Draga

claims.statement: It could fly, swim and walk, its fetid breath polluted the whole Gironès, and it devoured many animals and people.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat terbang, berenang, dan berjalan, napasnya yang busuk mencemari seluruh Gironès, dan ia memangsa banyak hewan dan manusia.
claims.quote: Podia volar, nedar i caminar i amb el seu alè fètid infestava tot el Gironès. Era el terror de la zona i es menjava molts animals i persones

claims.quote: Els cercadors de tresors anaven antigament equipats amb un mirall per tal d'esquivar el perill del basilisc, ja que aquest, en veure-s'hi reflectit, es moria víctima de la seva pròpia mirada.

claims.statement: Basiliscs were said to hatch from small green, red or blue eggs laid by cockerels, or from the vapour of gold, since that metal held the creature's seed.

claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, Bep-Kororoti adalah guru mitis yang diyakini orang Kayapó pernah mengunjungi leluhur mereka berabad-abad lalu, datang dari angkasa dengan pakaian berkilau, memberi banyak pengetahuan, dan mendirikan sekolah pertama.
claims.quote: Bep-Kororoti é um mítico professor que os índios Kayapó acreditam ter visitado seus ancestrais séculos atrás, vindo do espaço vestido com um terno brilhante, deu-lhes muito conhecimento e fundou a primeira escola.

claims.statement: João Américo Peret was the first to record in Portuguese the Kayapó legend of the creation of the world and the sky teacher Bep-Kororoti.
claims.statement_id: João Américo Peret adalah orang pertama yang mencatat dalam bahasa Portugis legenda Kayapó tentang penciptaan dunia dan guru langit Bep-Kororoti.
claims.quote: O Dr. João Américo Peret, eminente pesquisador brasileiro da cultura indígena, foi o primeiro a registrar no idioma português a antiga lenda dos índios Kavapo sobre a criação do mundo e o inusitado mestre celeste Bep-Kororoti.

claims.statement: In the legend warriors attacked the stranger in the shining suit, but poisoned arrows, spears and clubs bounced off him without harm.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda itu, para pejuang menyerang orang asing berpakaian berkilau ini, tetapi panah beracun, tombak, dan gada memantul darinya tanpa melukai.
claims.quote: Para seu total espanto, as flechas envenenadas, lanças e clavas simplesmente ricochetearam nele sem feri-lo.

claims.statement: The peaceful newcomer was called Bep-Kororoti, rendered as "I came from the sky", and he founded the first school, a house for young men, in the rainforest.
claims.statement_id: Pendatang damai itu disebut Bep-Kororoti, yang dapat diartikan "aku datang dari langit", dan ia mendirikan sekolah pertama, rumah bagi kaum muda, di hutan hujan.
claims.quote: A tradição diz que esse pacífico recém-chegado foi chamado Bep-Kororoti, que pode ser traduzido descritivamente como "eu vim do céu" ou "eu vim do espaço". Ele logo fundou a primeira escola - um lar para jovens - na floresta tropical

claims.statement: After years he climbed the hill of Pukato-Ti; there was a terrible roar, and the young men saw their teacher vanish into the air amid smoke and thunder.
claims.statement_id: Setelah bertahun-tahun ia mendaki bukit Pukato-Ti; terdengar dentuman dahsyat, dan para pemuda melihat guru mereka lenyap ke udara di tengah asap dan guntur.
claims.quote: Depois que Bep-Kororoti subiu a colina, houve um estrondo terrível, e os jovens aterrorizados viram de longe como seu professor desapareceu repentinamente no ar cercado por grandes línguas de pano, fumaça e forte trovão.

claims.statement: At the annual celebration in his memory, a Kayapó man is dressed head to foot in a straw costume made after Bep-Kororoti's bo (suit).
claims.statement_id: Dalam perayaan tahunan untuk mengenangnya, seorang anggota suku Kayapó dibalut dari kepala sampai kaki dengan pakaian jerami yang dibuat menurut bo (pakaian) Bep-Kororoti.
claims.quote: Nesta ocasião, um dos membros da tribo Kayapó está vestido da cabeça aos pés com uma roupa de palha cuidadosamente confeccionada segundo o bo de Bep-Kororoti.

claims.statement: The costume also resembles a beekeeper's suit, contrary to ufological theories.
claims.statement_id: Artikel itu sendiri mencatat bahwa pakaian ritual ini juga mirip pakaian peternak lebah, berlawanan dengan teori ufologi.
claims.quote: Nota: A vestimenta também se assemelha a um traje de apicultor. Contrariando as teorias ufologas.

claims.quote: La Bête à sept têtes est un type de monstre de légende qui se retrouve, sous des formes différentes (souvent un dragon ou un serpent à sept têtes) dans de nombreuses religions, mythologies et traditions à travers le monde. Dans plusieurs traditions, lorsqu'une tête est tranchée, elle repousse en un ou plusieurs exemplaires.

claims.statement: It appears in Christian mythology (the Beast of the Apocalypse), Hindu mythology (the nāga), Libyan mythology (the Talafsa), Basque mythology (Herensugue) and folk tales of many countries.

claims.quote: On retrouve la bête à sept têtes notamment dans la mythologie chrétienne (la Bête de l'Apocalypse), la mythologie hindoue (le nâga), la mythologie libyque (la Talafsa), la mythologie basque (Herensugue), ainsi que dans des contes populaires de divers pays

claims.statement: According to Revelation (17:9) its seven heads are the seven hills (of Rome) and at the same time seven successive kings.

claims.quote: Dans la mythologie berbère, le dragon féminin à sept têtes, Talafsa, contrôle l'eau d'une région et ne la donne qu'en échange du sacrifice annuel d'une jeune fille.

claims.statement: The seven-headed beast is a classic image of the dragon in many folk tales.

claims.quote: Le conte Ti-Jean et le cheval blanc, conte de la Beauce ayant pour héros Ti-Jean, héros par excellence des contes du Canada français, évoque aussi la Bête à sept têtes.

claims.statement: Bida protects Wagadu and the ruling Cissé family in exchange for the regular sacrifice of a girl, until he is killed by a man called Amadou as he is about to devour his yearly victim.

claims.statement: The death of the guardian serpent is generally used by the story to explain the kingdom's decline.

claims.statement: The serpent has many names: Bida or Miniyan in Soninke, Sâba in Mandinka, or Wagadou Sa ba, "great serpent of Wagadu".

claims.quote: Le serpent possède de nombreux noms différents selon les versions et les langues : Bida ou Miniyan en soninké, Sâba en mandinka, ou encore Wagadou Sa ba, « grand serpent du Ouagadou ».

claims.statement: Sometimes the sacrifice takes place every year at the end of the dry season, with the girl dressed in a white cloak and riding a white horse.

claims.statement: Before dying, the serpent lays a terrible curse on the land, promising seven years of drought.

claims.statement: Fragments of Bida's head fall in Bambouk and Bouré and turn into gold mines that later make the Ghana Empire prosper.

claims.quote: La biddrina è un animale mitico che secondo la leggenda vive nelle zone umide della campagna della provincia di Caltanissetta.

claims.statement: The name Biddrina may come from an Arabic word for a big water snake, or from 'belluino', bestial; in some parts of Sicily it is called Culobbia or Culofia.
claims.statement_id: Nama Biddrina mungkin berasal dari kata Arab untuk ular air besar, atau dari "belluino", buas; di beberapa daerah Sisilia ia disebut Culobbia atau Culofia.
claims.quote: Il termine Biddrina potrebbe derivare da una parola araba che indicherebbe un grosso serpente d'acqua. Secondo altre fonti, invece, potrebbe originare da "belluino", bestiale. In alcune zone della Sicilia viene chiamata Culobbia o "Culofia".

claims.statement: This ferocious reptile is green-blue with red eyes and a mouth big enough to swallow kids, lambs and children.
claims.statement_id: Reptil yang sangat buas ini berwarna antara hijau dan biru, bermata merah, dan bermulut begitu besar sehingga dapat menelan anak kambing, anak domba, dan anak-anak.
claims.quote: Questo ferocissimo rettile avrebbe una colorazione tra il verde e il blu, occhi rossi e una bocca talmente grande da consentirgli di ingoiare capretti, agnelli e bambini.

claims.statement: It has a sturdy armour of shining scales that makes it practically indestructible.
claims.statement_id: Ia berlapis sisik bercahaya yang kuat sehingga hampir tak dapat dihancurkan.
claims.quote: Possiede una robusta corazza di squame luminose che la rende praticamente indistruttibile.

claims.statement: In Butera, on the eve of the feast of San Rocco, people parade u sirpintazzu, a papier-mâché bogey like a Chinese dragon, to commemorate the killing of a Biddrina.

claims.quote: Attualmente a Butera, la vigilia della festa di San Rocco, è costume portare in giro per le strade u sirpintazzu, uno spauracchio in carta pesta simile per fattezze al drago della tradizione cinese, proprio per ricordare l'uccisione di una Biddrina

claims.statement: Legend says a grass snake that stays hidden for seven years turns into a biddrina, growing gigantic as if by magic.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, ular yang bersembunyi selama tujuh tahun berubah menjadi biddrina dan tumbuh raksasa seperti disihir.
claims.quote: La leggenda vuole che una biscia che rimanga nascosta per sette anni si tramuta in biddrina, diventando gigantesca come per magia.

claims.statement: Biliku is a legendary being worshipped in the Andaman Islands, often depicted as a spider-woman.

claims.statement: She is said to have existed before the world's creation and one day created the Earth and humans: after weaving her web, she stalked through the 'vast empty night'.
claims.statement_id: Konon ia ada sebelum dunia diciptakan dan suatu hari menciptakan bumi dan manusia: setelah menenun jaringnya, ia melangkah diam-diam dalam "malam kosong yang luas".
claims.quote: Si narra che esistesse prima della creazione del mondo e che un giorno creò la Terra e gli uomini: dopo aver tessuto la sua tela, si aggirò furtiva e a grandi passi nella "vasta notte vuota"

claims.statement: Pleased with her creation, she moved there bringing fire and light, governing everything, especially the weather, according to her mood.
claims.statement_id: Puas dengan ciptaannya, ia pindah ke bumi membawa api dan cahaya, dan mengatur segala hal, terutama cuaca, menurut suasana hatinya.
claims.quote: Contenta della sua creazione vi si trasferì, portandovi il fuoco e la luce e governandone ogni aspetto (in particolare il tempo atmosferico) a seconda del suo umore

claims.statement: The Bisso Galeto, also called El Cicolin Giacomo, is a legendary creature of the Verona valleys from Lessinia to Perzacco, with the body and head of a cockerel (galeto), a big red comb, spiny wings and a snake's tail (bisso).
claims.statement_id: Bisso Galeto, disebut juga El Cicolin Giacomo, adalah makhluk legendaris lembah-lembah Verona dari Lessinia sampai Perzacco, bertubuh dan berkepala ayam jantan (galeto) dengan jengger merah besar, sayap berduri, dan ekor ular (bisso).
claims.quote: Il Bisso Galeto Meglio chiamato El Cicolin Giacomo è una creatura leggendaria delle valli veronesi dalla Lessinia fino a Perzacco. Ha corpo e testa di gallo (galeto), con una grande cresta rossa, ali piene di spine e coda di serpente (bisso).

claims.statement: It can lengthen or shorten its body at will, is extremely venomous, and is said to hatch from an old cockerel's egg brooded by a snake or toad for nine years.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat memanjang dan memendekkan tubuhnya sesuka hati, sangat beracun, dan konon menetas dari telur ayam jantan tua yang dierami ular atau kodok selama sembilan tahun.
claims.quote: il Bisso Galeto può aumentare e diminuire la lunghezza del proprio corpo a sua volontà. È un animale velenosissimo. Nascerebbe da un uovo deposto da un gallo vecchio e covato da un serpente o da un rospo per nove anni.

claims.statement: Its gaze can kill, wither plants and taint water; its breath and bite are deadly.
claims.statement_id: Tatapannya dapat membunuh, mengeringkan tanaman, dan mencemari air; napas dan gigitannya mematikan.
claims.quote: Lo sguardo del Bisso Galeto può uccidere, seccare le piante e contaminare l'acqua. Il fiato e il morso del Bisso Galeto sono mortali.

claims.statement: If the Bisso sees its own reflection in a mirror, it dies.
claims.statement_id: Bila Bisso melihat bayangannya sendiri di cermin, ia mati.
claims.quote: Se il Bisso vede la propria immagine in uno specchio muore.

claims.statement: Its only natural enemies are weasels, which can kill it only at the cost of their own lives, and cockerels, whose crowing can kill it.
claims.statement_id: Musuh alaminya hanya musang, yang dapat membunuhnya dengan mengorbankan nyawa sendiri, dan ayam jantan yang dapat membunuhnya dengan kokoknya.
claims.quote: Gli unici "nemici naturali" del Bisso Galeto sono le donnole, che però possono ucciderlo solo a costo della propria vita e i galli che riescono a far morire il Bisso con il proprio canto.

claims.statement: A local legend blames the Bisso for the syphilis epidemic that spread through the Verona valleys in the 15th century.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah legenda setempat menyalahkan Bisso atas wabah sifilis di lembah-lembah Verona pada abad ke-15.
claims.quote: Una leggenda locale vuole che il Bisso sia stato causa dell'epidemia di sifilide diffusasi nelle valli veronesi nel XV secolo.

claims.statement: It shares many traits with the basilisk and is therefore sometimes confused with it.
claims.statement_id: Ia punya banyak ciri yang juga dimiliki basilisk, sehingga kadang tertukar dengannya.
claims.quote: Presenta molte caratteristiche ricorrenti anche nel basilisco, per questo viene a volte confuso con esso.
